description: DE line 11: a JOINT return on which only ONE spouse qualifies gets NOTHING, not $2,000. The printed worksheet offers exactly two columns and the joint column's first question is 'Were BOTH spouses at least 60 years old or totally and permanently disabled'; the booklet's note settles it — 'If you are filing a joint return and only one spouse qualifies for this exclusion, you should consider filing separate returns (Filing Status 3 or 4)', advice that would be pointless if the joint return already produced $2,000. Section 1106(b)(2) read alone might suggest the single $2,000; the form does not allow it.
